articles.title: Partial Eclipse at Houge Park Report
articles.summary: The June 10th partial solar eclipse at Houge Park was a significant success, drawing a large crowd with at least 30 telescopes set up for observation. The event featured a long-focus heliograph for solar projection and benefited from contributions by various observers and a 5th-grade class providing refreshments. The article also includes a detailed calendar of July and August activities for the San Jose Astronomical Association, listing star parties, ATM classes, and general meetings.

articles.title: Mooning Column
articles.summary: This article, primarily a column titled "Mooning," describes the author's experience at the RTMC Astronomy Expo, highlighting its primary value as a community gathering for amateur astronomers rather than just for new equipment, especially as an activity during a full Moon. It also briefly touches on a solar eclipse viewed during a new Moon. The document additionally includes a separate announcement detailing an upcoming Astronomical Society of the Pacific (ASP) lecture series and banquet, featuring several prominent astronomers and the presentation of annual awards.

articles.title: The Cosmic Threat: From Stars to Life
articles.summary: The Astronomical Society of the Pacific (ASP) is hosting its 114th Annual Meeting, themed "The Cosmic Thread: From Stars to Life," on September 28-29, 2002, in the San Francisco Bay Area. The event features a free public lecture by David H. Levy and a star party on Saturday, followed by a full day of lectures by leading astronomers at UC Berkeley on Sunday.
keywords: The Cosmic Threat: From Stars to Life

articles.title: Deep Sky for July
articles.summary: This article, "Deep Sky for July," by Mark Wagner, offers a guide to observing deep sky objects, primarily in Sagittarius, Cygnus, Vulpecula, and Lyra, during the first half of July. It details various celestial targets, including prominent globular clusters, galaxies, planetary nebulae, open clusters, and double stars, along with tips for viewing them using telescopes and binoculars, sometimes suggesting specific filters. The piece also encourages amateur astronomers to connect with local observing groups for shared learning and assistance.

articles.title: Starry Starry Nights in the Foothills
articles.summary: The article announces "Starry Starry Nights," a series of public star parties taking place over seven nights at different dark-sky locations in Northern California's foothills during Labor Day Week (August 28 - September 3), highlighting the Milky Way. Organized by Don Machholz and the Colfax Chamber of Commerce, astronomers are invited to participate with their telescopes. Additionally, the document includes a reader's recommendation for Dave Chandler's "Night Sky" planisphere and provides detailed directions to Houge Park in San Jose, a common site for public star parties.

articles.title: Davis Star Show, July 19-20
articles.summary: The Davis Star Show is seeking telescope owners to volunteer for a large public star party on July 20, 2002, expecting over 3,000 attendees. Volunteers will help people view the night sky and be entered into a drawing for a Stellarvue 80/9D High Resolution Refractor. Additionally, the article includes an announcement for an associate editor position at Astronomy magazine and an obituary for Rita Miram, a long-time SJAA member.

articles.title: SJAA Loaner Scope Status
articles.summary: This article outlines the status of the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) loaner telescope program, providing a comprehensive list of available scopes, those currently on loan with due dates, and those with extended loan periods. SJAA members can contact Mike Koop to borrow a scope, with a waiting list in place for popular models. The document also includes a note about a member's contribution to updating a scope.
